items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: Remoulade by Howard Jacobs. This write-up came about from the editor of Reader's Digest who asked Mr. Jacobs to find out about me, whether I was still living and what I was doing.

ctx.x: I want you to read this here about a nine-man court.

This is a nine-man court to hear appeal of Live Right from the New Orleans States Washington Bureau. They go on Washington. The appeal of Herman Live Right, former New Orleans television station director, from a contempt of Congress conviction, will be heard by the full nine-man United States Court of Appeals here, April 19... I'm sorry, April 23rd. The Live Right case, one of nine in a mass, but not consolidated hearing, will be taken up by the court at 10 a.m. Live Right and Allen bond were sentenced to three…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: I had told Mr. Howard Jacobs that's where this tune was born. He in turn laughed at it. ... Howard Jacobs is a man who writes Remmelade. He was sent here by the Newsweek people to find out if I was still living. ... And I explained to him where this tune was composed.

ctx.x: Yes, it's very clear and it's not rude.

I don't want to be rude. That's where that idea comes. I had told Mr. Howard Jacobs that's where this tune was born. He in turn laughed at it. But I'm telling you the truth of the tune. Where the tunes come in, my inability as a gifted musician, only having a few little ideas about me to put to use the different parts and make a number. I'll tie you on the cuff. I'll tie you on the cuff. I'll tie you on the cuff. Here we go. Howard Jacobs is a man who writes Remmelade. He was sent here by the Newsweek people to…

Now if there's any man living that knows anything about the Mopah Blues, which was played in New Orleans ten years before I went to Chicago, they'll attest to this tune when they hear it. With the exception of the introduction and the runs. The runs were made purposely so whoever on this tune could cry to sound something like the Liverstable Blues. Now we won the suit, we got the royalties from the Liverstable Blues, from the Victor people, and we are next to peace which I'm sorry to say that I didn't want. But…
